content: When product code does `import { fn } from 'node:fs/promises'` (or any module), `vi.spyOn(module, 'fn')` in the test does NOT intercept the call — the binding was resolved at import time. Put the test in a separate `*.test.ts` file with a module-level `vi.mock('node:fs/promises', async (importOriginal) => ({ ...actual, fn: ... }))`, so the mock cannot leak into the real-filesystem tests beside it.
context: Hit three times during ISS-027: the canonical-revalidation test (moved to workspace.canonical.test.ts), the preparation-timeout test (request-prep.timeout.test.ts), and the instruction-file-growth test (copilot-instructions.growth.test.ts). Each time the spy silently did nothing and the assertion failed for the wrong reason.
title: vi.spyOn cannot intercept a static ESM named import; mock the module in its own test file
